title: UV-vis-NIR quantification of Co( ii ), Ni( ii ) and HCl across acid-dependent speciation by multivariate analysis
content: Fiber-optic ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared (UV-vis-NIR) spectroscopy combined with data-efficient calibration designs and chemometric modeling enabled quantification of Co (0–100 mM) and Ni (0–100 mM) in HCl (0.1–6 M). This study highlights this method's potential for online monitoring in acid-dependent, speciation-sensitive processes relevant to the production of radioisotopes such as 63Ni. In this work, UV-vis and NIR absorption spectra were collected for ternary aqueous solutions containing Ni(ii), Co(ii), and HCl to evaluate how calibration set design influences multivariate prediction in a chemically overlapping system. Partial least squares regression was used as the primary calibration method to evaluate quantitative prediction from UV-vis and NIR spectra across several compact and structured calibration sets. Model performance was assessed using independent external validation sets, including a targeted low-concentration set within the calibrated range. Calibration design influenced predictive accuracy, but the best performing design was analyte-dependent, indicating that calibration set representativeness was more important than sample number alone. The D-optimal design, containing just 20 samples, often performed competitively for Ni(ii), Co(ii) and HCl despite requiring fewer calibration samples. This result indicated the method's practical value when standards are costly, hazardous, or limited. These results demonstrate that fiber-optic absorption spectroscopy paired with efficient calibration designs can support robust quantification in strongly acidic, compositionally complex solutions and may provide a useful strategy for process monitoring in radiochemical separations in which concentration and speciation are both important.
